summary.text: Liz Boldon is a Democratic state senator from Minnesota who represents District 25 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026.
She is a registered nurse who previously served in the Minnesota House of Representatives.

paragraphs.text: Boldon was born in Waterloo, Iowa, and earned a bachelor's degree from Allen College in 2002.

In a Ballotpedia survey, she said she has practiced as a registered nurse in the Neuroscience ICU and as float staff, earned a Master of Science in Nursing with a focus on education in 2008, and now works on an orthopedic and trauma general care unit.
Boldon represented District 25B in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2021 to 2023 and assumed office in the Minnesota State Senate on January 3, 2023, succeeding David Senjem (R).

In the survey she said she has been vice chair of the Housing and Homelessness Prevention Committee, serves as an Assistant Majority Leader, and co-chairs the Inclusive Democracy Caucus and the Minnesota Values Project in the Senate.
Boldon described healthcare, housing, democracy and child care as the focus of her legislative work and listed family economic security, healthcare and voting rights among her campaign messages.
In the 2026 general election she faces John Howie.
